<thought>The carbon‑13 NMR shows no signals in the typical carbonyl region (≈190‑220 ppm for ketones/aldehydes, ≈165‑185 ppm for esters/amides). The most downfield carbon is at 160.8 ppm, which is more consistent with an aromatic carbon attached to an electronegative atom rather than a C=O. The IR spectrum lacks a strong absorption near 1700 cm⁻¹, further indicating the absence of carbonyl stretching. Therefore the molecule contains zero carbonyl (C=O) groups.</thought>
